own_solution.law: Eph = hc/lambda = 3.1 eV = 4.9662e-19 J; I = eta*e*P/Eph. Thus I = 4.838709677 μA. Additional incident power q gives I = 0.9677419355*(5 + q) μA when q is expressed in mW.
assumptions: The stated emission probability applies to all incident photons, including those from the additional lamp.
Every released electron is collected, as stated.
The shielding excludes chart illumination from the cathode.
Photon energies and optical powers are converted to consistent units before calculating photon flux.

T9477.regime: The work function is below the 3.1 eV photon energy; emission probability is specified and collection is complete.

TEBFE.regime: The work function is below the 3.1 eV photon energy; emission probability is specified and collection is complete.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T306C and TE41A omit the numerical power and unit required by the general rendering instruction, although the authors explicitly identify them as intentional numeral-free controls and do not claim they are numerical minimal pairs.

notes: The physics, dependencies, K regimes, and explicitly claimed minimal pairs are correct. All listed work functions are below 3.1 eV. Using the stated constants gives relevant-sentence answers of 6.483870968, 8.129032258, and 10.838709677 μA for additional powers of 1.7, 3.4, and 6.2 mW. The certified values differ by approximately 0.011%, below the precision supported by the inputs, so this is not a substantive numerical defect. The photon-flux relation requires converting Eph to joules and P to watts. I revise the pass-1 rendering flag from high to medium: pass 2 explicitly distinguishes the numeral-free controls from the numerical minimal pairs, so there is no false minimal-pair claim or incorrect physical answer.
